scenes.heading: Reading a creative brief without missing requirements

sents.d: Reading a creative brief without missing requirements
Missed brief details are the most common reason for revision requests.

A creative brief typically specifies the hook or opening line, key talking points, tone, required shots, and technical specs (length, aspect ratio, captions on/off) — missing any of these is the most common reason for a revision request that costs you time.
Making a simple checklist from each brief before you shoot, rather than trying to hold every requirement in your head, catches gaps before they become a reshoot.

When a brief is genuinely unclear on something important (the intended platform, a specific claim to include or avoid), asking a clarifying question before shooting is far cheaper than guessing wrong and reshooting.

take: Checklist every brief and clarify before shooting.
